title: Seed agent permissions without mutating repository-controlled paths
description:
## Finding

Resolving any local agent launch performs a host-authority read/modify/write of `<worktree>/.claude/settings.local.json` before sandbox preparation or trust admission. The worktree and both path components are repository-controlled.

The seeder follows an existing `.claude` symlink and follows the final `settings.local.json` symlink. If the final target does not exist, the initial read treats it as an ordinary missing settings file and `std::fs::write` creates the symlink target. A candidate checkout can therefore redirect the host process into creating or overwriting a JSON file outside the worktree. The write is also non-atomic and generation-unfenced.

Even without a redirect, Thegn alters the candidate working tree before the worker starts and never restores the prior bytes. That can dirty the branch, make the completion clean-tree gate fail, or cause an agent to commit local capability policy into the product change. A write failure is warning-only, so a headless worker is launched even though the requested permission contract was not installed.

## Evidence at audited commit `299fc13`

* `crates/thegn-host/src/agent.rs:3297-3316` calls the seeder before repository-root resolution, sandbox preparation, and any later launch admission. It applies to every local launch with a non-empty effective permission list and deliberately continues after errors.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/agent_permissions.rs:18-24` maps Claude to the fixed repository-relative path `.claude/settings.local.json`.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/agent_permissions.rs:61-84` reads by pathname, recursively creates the parent, and rewrites with `std::fs::write`; it performs no root containment, no-follow, inode/type/link-count, ownership, lock, generation, atomicity, durability, or restoration checks.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/cmd/session.rs:915-920,1017-1042` documents this seeder as the mechanism that makes stage-level permissions effective for a headless pipeline dispatch.
* `docs/help/configuration.md:246` and `crates/thegn-core/src/config.rs:1770` advertise the mutation as the public `permissions` behavior, but do not disclose the candidate-tree mutation, persistence, or warning-only failure semantics.

A tracked symlink `.claude/settings.local.json -> /chosen/missing.json`, or a tracked `.claude` symlink to an outside directory, is enough to move the write out of the worktree. Because Git records symlinks, merely checking out a branch can supply the redirect before Thegn launches its worker.

## Impact

* Repository content can cause the privileged host process to create or overwrite an outside JSON path before containment.
* Concurrent launches/readers can observe truncated JSON or lose each other's policy changes.
* Thegn's own launch preparation dirties the implementation branch and can contaminate commits, reviews, and completion gates.
* Headless tasks can run under a different tool policy from the resolved configuration while the roster still describes the intended agent/stage.
* Permission changes persist beyond the session and silently affect later manual agent launches in the same worktree.

## Dependency mapping

This issue blocks <issue id="f94f8554-b48e-47e8-a672-27e208e0dc48" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-233/credential-isolate-every-autonomous-issue-merge-pr-ci-and-review-agent">THE-233</issue>: autonomous-agent credential isolation cannot be considered complete while pre-launch preparation gives candidate paths a host write primitive and launches on policy-install failure.

It is related to <issue id="970df36c-bf76-4f4b-9e01-51b279e22c00" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-434/stop-trusted-project-hooks-from-executing-mutable-branch-code-with">THE-434</issue> (mutable project harness authority), <issue id="1b0f9f75-b333-495c-86d8-b5bd273087d4" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-225/fence-sandbox-git-writes-from-hooks-and-host-executed-control-metadata">THE-225</issue> (candidate-controlled Git/worktree metadata crossing into later host actions), <issue id="170ba4b4-3f08-4ec4-8d80-c14cdc8da795" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-371/make-git-config-self-healing-no-follow-atomic-and-race-safe">THE-371</issue> (no-follow generation-fenced configuration writes), and <issue id="3d3a566c-145a-4f99-a005-3a6e739f4753" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-268/bind-pipeline-claim-prompt-and-sandbox-launch-to-one-immutable-config">THE-268</issue> (claim and launch must use one immutable effective policy).

## Required implementation

1. Do not mutate repository-controlled harness settings as an implicit launch side effect. Prefer a host-owned, per-session, immutable settings overlay or a harness-native command/environment mechanism outside the candidate tree.
2. Bind the overlay to the exact dispatch/session, effective config revision, agent identity, worktree identity, and candidate commit.
3. If a harness absolutely requires a project-local file, pin the worktree root by handle, reject symlinks/reparse points at every component, require a regular owner-controlled leaf, lock and generation-check existing bytes, publish atomically/durably, and restore exactly on every exit/error/crash path. Do not touch tracked content without explicit consent.
4. Make effective-policy installation a fail-closed launch precondition for headless stages. Publish the installed policy digest with the roster/session attestation.
5. Separate user-managed settings from Thegn-generated transient policy; preserve all user keys and concurrent edits without a read/modify/write race.
6. Keep remote/provider launches semantically equivalent without host-tree mutation or silent omission.

## Acceptance criteria

* Tests use a final symlink, symlinked `.claude` directory, reparse point, missing symlink target, FIFO/device, hard link, non-owner target, and component-swap race; none can write outside the exact admitted root.
* A normal permissioned launch leaves `git status --porcelain=v1 -z` byte-for-byte unchanged before, during, and after the session.
* Concurrent launches with different policies cannot overwrite, merge, or inherit one another's grants.
* Failed policy creation, validation, publication, or attestation prevents a headless process from spawning and records an infrastructure/policy hold rather than task failure.
* Crash/kill/restart tests prove no persistent widening remains.
* The worker and verifier can attest the exact effective allow/deny policy and config/candidate generation used for that run.
* Existing user settings, comments/format where relevant, deny rules, hooks, and unknown fields remain untouched.
* Documentation and schemas state the supported per-harness behavior and fail-closed semantics.
